verdict.rationale: ObsessionDB documents that it runs the official ClickHouse engine with the same SQL, and that every query works unchanged. That implies the stock ClickHouse analytical SQL surface is available natively, not through extensions. However, the evidence pack never names window functions, CTEs, JSON, arrays or date/time types, so the specific elements of the story rest on a general compatibility claim. missing for 10: explicit documentation of window functions, CTEs, semi-structured JSON type support, array functions, rich date/time types, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an analyst, I get a full analytical SQL surface — window functions, CTEs, semi-structured JSON, arrays, and rich date/time types — without bolt-on extensions

citations.quote: ObsessionDB runs the official ClickHouse engine on a rebuilt storage layer with compute–storage separation.
Every query, every client, every tool you already use works unchanged. If you know ClickHouse, you know ObsessionDB.
